_roles_note: Explicit, so renaming a zone later cannot silently change what it measures. 'reception' carries seating too: this venue has no separate seating area, and without it the zone-completeness guard reports a missing role every run -- a warning that is always wrong gets ignored. 'plant area mask' MUST keep the word mask: _drop_masked deletes detections whose feet land inside a mask zone, and that is the only thing stopping the plant becoming 'P13 staff'.

_how: RENAME to 'ground_points' once real. Needs >=5 ADJACENT floor-tile corners (no skips, no duplicates) plus the tile edge in cm. 4 points fit ANY labelling with zero error -- see tools/calibrate_plane.py enough_evidence().

_main_entrance_note:
EXTENDED TO THE FRAME BOTTOM 2026-08-15, from measurement not opinion.
Across 8,219 recorded boxes in a 10-minute run, main_entrance scored ZERO hits while reception scored 460, dining 660 and waiting 305. The 284 foot-points on the entrance side sat at y p10 1078 / p50 1079 / max 1084 (analysis space, frame is 1080 tall) — i.e. ON THE FRAME BOTTOM, because a person at that door is in the extreme foreground and their box is clipped by the frame edge. The old polygon stopped at y1072. Seven pixels was the whole difference between 0 hits and 284.
x also pulled from 1354 to 1300 (file 2600): observed foot x had p10 1326, so the left edge was clipping the approach as well.
GENERAL LESSON for any camera: an ENTRY zone must reach the frame edge. People arrive from off-camera, so their first frames are always clipped, and a zone that stops short of the border can never see an arrival.
_geometry_note:
NAMES SWAPPED 2026-08-14 on operator correction. The polygon on the RIGHT (x2708-3828) is the STREET ENTRANCE — that is where in/out happens. The bottom-left region is the DINING area, not an entrance; learn_zones clustered 12 births and 12 deaths there because guests LEAVE frame toward dining, which looks identical to arriving unless you know the room.
Consequence of the old naming: the region arrival method counted anyone walking into DINING as a venue arrival, and 'entry' role on both sides meant there was no cross-check at all — just the same error twice.
The LINES were already correct: 'entry line' is on the right, 'dining entry' bottom-left. Only the polygons were mislabelled.
_plant_mask_note: EXTENDED TO THE FLOOR AGAIN 2026-08-14. y stopped at 1824; the plant's detection box has its feet near y2320, and _drop_masked tests the box's BOTTOM edge — so the plant escaped its own mask and came back as a tracked person (P8, blue, 06:33 PM). A mask that triggers on feet has to reach the floor. Wide across the foliage, narrowing to the pot, so it does not eat the walkable floor either side.
_entry_lines_flip_note:
WHICH SIDE IS 'IN', PER DOOR. A LineZone's direction comes from the ORDER of its two points — i.e. from the direction the mouse was dragged. One global ENTRY_LINE_FLIP for three hand-drawn doors cannot be right for all three: flipping it to fix the entrance inverts dining and the staff gate.
These start at the old global value (True) so this run reproduces the last one exactly. Then check the annotated video, which now labels EACH door with its OWN count, and flip the ones that read backwards. A door where people obviously walked in but OUT went up is inverted — flip that one only.
_entry_lines_confirm_note:
CONFIRMATION WAIT per door, seconds. A crossing counts only if the person was still on the far side after this long; cross back sooner and BOTH events are cancelled, because nobody arrived or left.
Per door because the doors do not behave alike: the street ENTRY LINE sits exactly where guests pause to be greeted, so it needs the longest wait (6s). Dining is a walk-through (3s). The staff gate is used constantly and a long wait there would erase real movement (2s).
Raise a door's value if its count is too high; lower it if real crossings are being dropped. The run logs how many were cancelled per door.
